straitStatus.description: Strait remains severely restricted with ~65% traffic below pre-war levels (UKMTO Nov 18 report). diplomacy.headline: Iran-Oman negotiations advance; US-Qatar mediators seeking implementation of Iranian two-day reopening proposal

Iran proposed two-day implementation plan conditional on US compliance; Qatar mediators holding discussions but no breakthrough achieved to date.

alternativeRoutes.currentUsageStatus: Operating at ~1.5 mbpd capacity; limited incremental export option; underutilization vs potential.

news.title: Iran's Surface-To-Air Missile Hits F-16 Over Qeshm; US Jet Plunges To 4,500 Feet, Diverts To UAE
news.description: Fresh details have emerged about a reported Iranian missile attack on a US F-16 Fighting Falcon operating near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran allegedly fired a surface-to-air missile at the American fighter jet over Qeshm Island as tensions escalated following an Iranian anti-ship missile launch towards vessels escorted by the US Navy. The US F-16 subsequently squawked emergency code 7700 near the UAE at an altitude of 32,200 feet. Flight-tracking data reportedly showed the fighter jet plunging nearly 28,000 feet to around 4,500 feet, raising questions about the extent of the damage sustained during the confrontation. The aircraft reportedly managed to land safely at Al Dhafra Air Base in Abu Dhabi. The incident marks a potentially significant escalation in the confrontation between US forces and Iran around the strategically crucial Strait of Hormuz, raising fresh questions about Iranian air defence capabilities and the safety of American military aircraft operating in the region.

data.summary: President Trump signed an executive order requiring federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House of congressional information requests, coordinate on "appropriate responses," and withhold communications deemed privileged. items.name: Afghanistan-Pakistan War Tracker
items.headline: TTP Ambush Kills 10 Police in Kohat as Border Clashes Persist
items.subtitle: A TTP ambush in Kohat on November 11 killed 10 Pakistani police and, per police, 18 militants. Pakistan–Taliban border clashes continued into early November at Torkham, Angoor Adda and Kurram. Each side blames the other and casualty claims are unverified.

items.name: Bolivia Crisis Tracker
items.headline: Santa Cruz transport conditions Oct 5-6 strike on meeting with ministers as Morales' Decree 5716 deadline expires
items.subtitle: As of Oct. 3, Santa Cruz transport leaders were awaiting a meeting with the government on repealing Decree 5716 before deciding whether to strike for 48 hours from Oct. 5. Evo Morales' Oct. 3 repeal deadline lapses, with a national mobilization announced from Oct. 13.

items.name: Chile: History & Governance
items.headline: Kast Drops His Security Reform as Senators File a 30-Day State-of-Exception Alternative
items.subtitle: The government withdrew its constitutional security reform on October 6, and on October 7 senators from RN, Republicanos, DC and PPD filed a replacement that caps a state of exception at 30 days with congressional approval for extensions; the executive backs it, but it needs 29 Senate votes. The 2027 budget, submitted September 30, goes to the mixed committee for votes on October 26-28.

items.name: Cuba Crises Tracker
items.headline: Rubio Says US Hopeful Cuba Will Choose Different Political Path
items.subtitle: Tracking the Cuban Revolution, Cold War confrontations, US embargo, Soviet collapse, and Cuba's ongoing political and economic crises from 1959 to the present — now including the 2026 US energy blockade that has triggered an eighth nationwide grid collapse, a fresh round of US sanctions, and a record 1,339 political prisoners

items.name: DRC Conflict Tracker
items.headline: U.S. Imposes New Sanctions on Rwanda Over M23 Conflict in Congo
items.subtitle: The Health Ministry reports 4,018 Ebola deaths among about 8,300 confirmed cases, with Ituri the hardest-hit province. Fighting between government forces and M23 continues despite peace agreements, as the Security Council warned on Sept 29.

items.name: Ebola Outbreak Tracker
items.headline: Africa CDC Warns Congo's Ebola Outbreak Is Not Under Control as Cases Pass 11,200
items.subtitle: Government data show over 11,200 confirmed cases and 5,500 deaths across eight DRC provinces as of 15 November; over 80% of new cases arise outside contact lists.

items.name: Ethiopia Conflict Tracker
items.headline: Eritrea and Ethiopia Trade War Accusations as Tigray Rebels Retreat
items.subtitle: TPLF calls its pullout from Tigray's capital tactical and vows to keep fighting; fighting has spread to Afar and Amhara and Ethiopia-Eritrea relations are severed. Independent verification remains limited.

items.name: France: A Complete History
items.headline: Cyberattack on La Poste Subsidiary Maileva Exposes Data of 22 Million People
items.subtitle: From Clovis I and the Frankish kingdom (481 CE) to Macron's Fifth Republic — tracking the complete arc of French history: 13 dynasties, 5 republics, 2 empires, and the world's most influential political tradition.

items.name: Gaza War Tracker
items.headline: Israel Ends Central Gaza Ground Operation, First Since Ceasefire; 3 Killed Near Bureij and Nuseirat
items.subtitle: Israeli tanks pushed into central Gaza on Nov 18 near Al-Bureij and Nuseirat, killing three Palestinians per hospital officials; the IDF said it targeted a tunnel west of the Yellow Line and declared the operation complete on Nov 19. Hamas called it a flagrant ceasefire violation; eyewitnesses dispute that roads reopened.

items.name: Global Recession Risk Tracker
items.headline: S&P 500 and Dow Enter Correction, Nasdaq Erases 2026 Gain as AI Selloff Hits Despite Hawkish Fed
items.subtitle: On Nov 20 the S&P 500 and Dow closed about 10% below their highs and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026 as investors sold AI stocks after the Anthropic IPO. Treasuries rallied (10-year 4.93%, 2-year 4.63%), yet futures still priced about a 92% chance of a 25bp December hike. October FOMC minutes showed near-consensus for further hikes, and Governor Waller said a half-point move may be needed.

items.name: Haiti Collapse Tracker
items.headline: Haiti Postpones December 13 Elections as Salvadoran Troops Search for Four Missing Technicians
items.subtitle: On October 18 gangs attacked a Salvadoran Gang Suppression Force armored vehicle with explosives; four Salvadoran technicians remain missing and more than 2,000 Salvadoran troops have reportedly been sent to Haiti. The electoral council has postponed the December 13 vote and announced new dates of July 18 and October 4.

items.name: Hormuz Food & Energy Security Crisis Tracker
items.headline: Two Ships Hit Near Oman in Hormuz; Iran Says Vessel Caught Fire After Mine Strike
items.subtitle: Reports of tanker fires on Nov 13-14 are unverified; freight, insurance and import-cost risks rise

items.name: ICE History Tracker
items.headline: ICE Deportations and Arrests Hit Record High, CBS News Reports
items.subtitle: Released footage documents the moment an ICE vehicle struck a man during enforcement operations in Houston, amplifying scrutiny of immigration agency use-of-force practices.

items.name: India: 4,600 Years of Civilization
items.headline: Thousands Rally in New Delhi as INDIA Bloc Demands Election Chief's Resignation Over Electoral Roll Revision
items.subtitle: Historic Indian state elections reshape the political map: BJP wins West Bengal for the first time in party history, Kerala's last communist government falls, and film star Vijay's new TVK party ends 59 years of Dravidian dominance in Tamil Nadu — as India marks one year since Operation Sindoor.

items.name: India Youth Uprising Tracker
items.headline: Supreme Court issues notice on SIR petition, seeks Election Commission records
items.subtitle: The Cockroach Janta Party went ahead with its Oct 2 Gandhi Jayanti protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park despite police denying permission, and Mumbai Police have since registered a case against organisers. The movement, which began over the NEET-UG paper leak and CBSE marking irregularities, now centres on demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over the electoral-roll revision; Delhi Police separately registered three FIRs over anti-CEC protests with no individuals named. The CJP has said it plans to expand demonstrations nationwide.

items.name: Iran: 2,500-Year History
items.headline: Iran Sets Red Lines for US Talks: Sanctions Relief First, Enriched Uranium Stays
items.subtitle: Tehran says it will negotiate only if the US lifts sanctions and ends threats, and that no enriched uranium will leave the country. The White House says it will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms.

items.name: Iran Conflict Tracker
items.headline: Bahrain Accuses Iran of Attacking Its Territory to Settle Score With US; Saudi Arabia Joins Condemnation
items.subtitle: Nov 9, 2026: After meeting Qatar's PM, Trump says the war is effectively over while keeping the naval and 'Iron Gate' land blockades; Rubio says no breakthrough is near and Iran stands by its seven demands.

items.name: Lebanon: Full History
items.headline: Lebanon to Join Trilateral Talks with Israel and US in Florida Next Week, Aoun Says
items.subtitle: Israel detonated ~1,100 tons of explosives on Sep 10 to destroy a two-decade-old Hezbollah tunnel network beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge, a blast Netanyahu called a 'massive victory' and paired with a warning of 'heavier blows' if Hezbollah attacks again. Nightly strikes, artillery and house demolitions continued in al-Mansouri, Kfartebnit and other southern towns through Sep 17, with Israeli drones also spotted over Beirut. President Aoun visited Nabatieh on Sep 12, ruling out new talks with Israel 'at the moment' as the Rome round was postponed to October in favor of a lower-level Washington ambassadors' meeting on Sep 16. Domestically, a prosecutor asked on Sep 15 that former president Michel Aoun be charged over the 2020 Beirut port blast, and Hezbollah MPs clashed with rivals in parliament on Sep 16 over the party's arms.

items.name: Mecca Defense Pact Tracker
items.headline: Turkey Ratifies Mecca Defence Pact, Clearing Way for Military Support to Saudi Arabia
items.subtitle: Houthi cross-border strikes are now disrupting flight routes and airspace used by pilgrims traveling to Mecca, broadening the humanitarian and religious impact of the ongoing conflict.

items.name: mRNA Revolution Tracker
items.headline: BioNTech mRNA Cancer Vaccine Fails Phase 3 Trial, Rattling Oncology Confidence
items.subtitle: On August 5, the FDA approved Moderna's mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010) for adults 50+ — the first mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine ever licensed in the US, with full approval for ages 50-64 and accelerated approval for ages 65+, following a unanimous 9-0 VRBPAC vote on June 18 that reversed a February 2026 refusal-to-file. The approval came days after BioNTech named Guido Oelkers, ex-CEO of Sobi, to succeed co-founder Ugur Sahin as CEO by February 2027 (Aug 3), with Sahin departing to launch a new mRNA startup; BioNTech's Aug 4 Q2 results showed revenue down 59% on weak COVID demand but continued oncology pipeline progress (pumitamig 47.6% ORR in PD-L1-negative NSCLC). Separately, Moderna disclosed on July 31 that its mRNA-1403 norovirus vaccine missed a Phase 3 interim efficacy bar, extending the NOVA 301 trial into a third season.

items.name: Nicaragua Constitutional Crisis Tracker
items.headline: OAS Foreign Ministers Demand Nicaragua Free Prisoners and Restore Liberties
items.subtitle: On Oct. 2 the OAS adopted by consensus a resolution calling for free elections, release of political prisoners and disclosure of the disappeared, with a task force to recommend steps within 60 days. Mexico stayed out, Brazil and Uruguay objected to the 'threat to peace' wording, and the Dominican Republic is closing its Managua embassy.

items.name: North Korea / DPRK Tracker
items.headline: North Korea Says It Tested Air-Defence Missile, Staged Cruise Missile Drill
items.subtitle: North Korea deepens its alignment with Moscow as Kim Jong Un pledges renewed military and political support for Russia, while simultaneously warning the United States over Taiwan — signaling a coordinated shift in Pyongyang's foreign posture.

items.name: Global Peace Processes Tracker
items.headline: Russia-Ukraine Abu Dhabi Talks End With Prisoner-Swap Deal in Principle but No Ceasefire Breakthrough
items.subtitle: November 11, 2026 — Two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, the first Russia-Ukraine round since February, ended with an agreement in principle on a large prisoner exchange that Russian officials say could occur within two to three weeks. There was no progress on a ceasefire, territory or security guarantees, and Europe was excluded from the room. US envoys Kushner and Witkoff plan to meet Putin in Moscow and then Zelenskyy.

items.name: Poland Political Crisis Tracker
items.headline: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal Crisis Escalates as Nawrocki and Tusk Clash
items.subtitle: After the Tribunal's president was suspended on 30 Oct, President Nawrocki entered the court, new judges were seated and riot police clashed with protesters. Separately, the suspect in the October plot against PM Tusk remains charged with nine offences; no foreign link has been reported.

items.name: Pope Leo Health Crisis
items.headline: Pope Leo, in Uruguay, Cites His Own Illness to Urge Universal Health Care
items.subtitle: On October 13, 2026, the Vatican disclosed that a nodule removed from Pope Leo's lung during surgery was found to be malignant. The Vatican had initially confirmed the surgery was successful before revealing the cancerous diagnosis — a major development with global implications for the Catholic Church and 1.4 billion Catholics worldwide.

items.name: Sudan Civil War Tracker
items.headline: Britain Sanctions Sudanese Commanders Over Weaponised Rape as Drone Strikes Cut Power in the East
items.subtitle: A diplomatic crisis erupted around the UN General Assembly this week: US advisor Massad Boulos met Egyptian and Sudanese foreign ministers in New York on September 20, 2026 to press for a durable peace path, then the State Department withheld Sovereignty Council chief Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan's UNGA visa on September 22, tying it to a 90-day ceasefire Burhan rejected as a take-it-or-leave-it proposal — spokesman Tommy Pigott declared that neither SAF nor RSF have legitimate authority to rule Sudan, saying both 'rule through force of arms alone.' Sudan's UN ambassador asked Secretary-General Guterres to intervene, and on September 23 Burhan published a Foreign Policy op-ed proposing a Sudanese-led alternative centered on a single unified national army and rejecting political parity for the RSF. The diplomacy unfolded against continued fighting on the ground: a Rapid Support Forces attack on the Umm Badr gold market in North Kordofan killed five civilians and wounded 27 on September 21, days after the army's September 17 and 19 recapture of a dozen North Kordofan areas including the al-Jamama commercial hub. Day 1258 of the SAF-RSF war with no ceasefire and famine conditions persisting across Darfur and Kordofan.

items.name: Ukraine History Tracker
items.headline: Russian Drones Hit Kyiv Embassies and St. Volodymyr's Cathedral; Kerch Bridge Struck Again
items.subtitle: A hours-long drone raid on Kyiv on Nov 19 killed one person, injured five and damaged the Dutch and Austrian embassies and St. Volodymyr's Cathedral. Ukraine's Air Force counted 98 drones plus Onyx missiles overnight, after Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge on Nov 17.

items.name: Ukraine War Tracker
items.headline: Kushner Says Trump 'Open to the Idea' of NATO Protection for Ukraine
items.subtitle: Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles and drones overnight into September 24, killing 2 and injuring 8 and damaging Maternity Hospital No. 2 and the historic 1906 St. Pokrovsky Church, then hit the capital again overnight into September 25 with a mass drone barrage across six districts plus Brovary and Lutsk, killing 7 — including two children — and injuring 59. Ukraine responded on September 25 with long-range drone strikes on the Lukoil oil refinery in Perm (~1,450km inside Russia, 1 killed), the Iskra defense-electronics plant in Ulyanovsk (8 injured) and the Voronezhsintezkauchuk synthetic-rubber and rocket-propellant plant in Voronezh (13 injured); Russia claimed 592 drones intercepted overnight. Separately, Russian drones struck a medical center and ambulances in Zaporizhzhia on September 25, injuring 1. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,525,570 by September 25, per the Ukrainian General Staff. On September 26, Russia's FM Lavrov declared the war would continue 'through to the end,' China unveiled a peace plan signaling a diplomatic posture shift, and Zelensky said Russia shows no readiness to stop as Ukraine and allies plan additional pressure. On October 1, Russia launched its largest combined ballistic missile and drone attack on Ukraine's energy grid in months, killing at least 7 and causing widespread power cuts across the country. On October 2, Ukraine claimed the first combat use of its domestically produced FP-7 ballistic missile against Russia, while Putin praised PM Modi's peace initiative and Ukraine sought to mend diplomatic ties with South Korea over North Korea tensions. On October 3, Russia launched strikes targeting Kyiv bridges, causing significant traffic disruption across the Ukrainian capital.

items.name: United States — National Intelligence Dashboard
items.headline: Democrats Take Control of Congress in Midterms, Major Setback for Trump
items.subtitle: A week after Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over their coverage, US District Judge Timothy Kelly — a Trump first-term nominee — ordered their access temporarily restored on September 24, finding the outlets had been denied notice or a chance to be heard. The same week, the Senate rejected a 14th War Powers resolution on Iran 49-50 after Trump told the UN General Assembly he could 'annihilate' the Islamic Republic, Xi Jinping's state visit brought a two-month extension of the US-China tariff truce and a White House state dinner, and the Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years (to 3.75–4.00%) as August payrolls surged 162,000 and core inflation stayed firm. The Supreme Court also restored the administration's mass voter verification system on September 25, and the White House canceled roughly $810 million in congressionally approved HHS and related spending via a contested 'pocket rescission.'

items.name: US Measles Resurgence Tracker
items.headline: PAHO formally strips US of measles elimination status; 5,412 cases in 2026
items.subtitle: PAHO's director accepted the commission's recommendation on Nov 17, withdrawing elimination status from the US, Mexico and Bolivia. CDC counts 5,412 confirmed 2026 cases (+230 in the Nov 13 update), 96% outbreak-associated; CDC lists 6 deaths while states report 10.

items.name: US Interventions in Latin America
items.headline: Cuba Energy Crisis Peaks; CIA Director Ratcliffe Makes Rare Havana Visit as US Oil Blockade Empties the Island
items.subtitle: Cuba exhausted all fuel reserves by May 14, 2026 — 20–22 hour blackouts nationwide — as CIA Director Ratcliffe flew to Havana for secret talks with Cuban intelligence in the highest-level US-Cuba contact in decades. Meanwhile US Treasury escalated pressure on Nicaragua (Ortega sons + gold sector sanctioned) and Paraguay became the first Latin American country to accept US third-country deportees. Tracking 125+ years of coups, CIA operations, and Monroe Doctrine continuity from Operation PBSUCCESS to Operation Absolute Resolve.

news.title: Iran has a large underground network used to conceal and protect military assets, including missile capabilities.
news.summary: Its threats of a new war raise the risk of further escalation, while the conflict has shown that underground facilities can be difficult to locate and strike. IRGC Aerospace Forces Commander Majid Mousavi reported to his superior that his units are ready to carry out any order from the Supreme Commander. According to Mousavi, between rounds of military confrontation, Iran significantly expanded its missile capabilities and developed new weapons capable of delivering unpleasant surprises to the enemy. This is already the second such demonstration in eleven days. On November 10, Iranian television showed tunnels with ballistic and cruise missiles, launchers, and military equipment. At that time, the complex was inspected by Chief of the General Staff Ali Abdollahi and Mousavi. Now the IRGC commander-in-chief himself appeared in front of the cameras. Whether this refers to the same facility is unknown. Iranian military do not disclose their locations or disclose when the structures were built. From the published videos, it is impossible to judge how far the restoration of Iran's missile potential has progressed after American and Israeli bombings.

news.title: Here we go again
news.summary:
French protests losing momentum

The sixth Saturday of protests in France takes place under tight security, though turnout continues to decline steadily. On November 21, authorities deployed 70,000 police and gendarmes across the country, while Paris expects only 15 to 30 thousand demonstrators.

According to the Interior Ministry, across the country — excluding Paris — authorities recorded 44 actions that drew only 2,200 people. A week earlier at the same time, 9,800 demonstrators took to the streets in the regions.

At the moment, Paris remains relatively calm, with Lyon becoming the main flashpoint, where the prefecture banned demonstrations in the city center and mobilized a thousand security forces. Despite the ban, three unsanctioned columns started there.

Shortly after, CRS special forces deployed tear gas to stop the march at the Garibaldi metro station, while demonstrators managed to erect a barricade on Thermes Street. Overall, the Interior Ministry describes the situation across the country as calm: only seven people have been detained so far compared to 24 a week ago.

📌Turnout has noticeably declined, the Saturday protest format is clearly running out of steam. Nevertheless, authorities are not easing up, as the protest remains politically unresolved. Trade unions have already scheduled a new strike for December 1, while presidential elections in April 2027 loom increasingly large on the agenda.

The protesters clearly are not waiting for concessions from the current government — they are formulating demands to present to the next cabinet. Only a change in power is unlikely to change anything.

news.title: Iranians, disinformation, two tankers
news.summary:
The information wave around the Strait of Hormuz turned out to be a bubble again. Yesterday, Iranian and Israeli media outlets were "promoting" reports about Iranian ships allegedly heading to sea, supposedly preparing to "head-on" break through the American naval blockade. However, by evening, the Islamic Republic's media published denials.

In addition, maritime tracker data showed only three vessels in the waters, and none of them were tankers or combat ships. These were a cargo ship, a pleasure yacht off the coast of Bushehr, and a tugboat, presumably heading to Keshm.

🖍Theoretically, the Iranians could have used such disinformation to test the waters and, against the backdrop of Donald Trump's visit to China, assess the American response and how tightly the blockade is actually being maintained.

Moreover, Tehran could have genuinely attempted to send a couple of tankers to break through as a test run. Such sorties have occurred in their practice. If the vessels pass through, the Iranians would get excellent proof that there is no American blockade as such. If they are stopped – there will be another round of strikes and demonstrative hits, for example, on targets in Kuwait or Bahrain, which is also, on the whole, acceptable.

❗️On the other hand, the rumor of a "breakthrough" benefits the Israelis, who are pushing the situation toward a major war. The image of Iranian aggression in the strait is needed for the American administration, which acting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his people in the intelligence service have been urging for months to launch a new campaign.

news.title: The ambassador knocks on every door
news.summary:
While Washington closes its wallet and reads the riot act, Moscow opens an embassy and embraces the security forces. French observers documented a series of Russian meetings in South Sudan, and the contact list reads like a manual for capturing influence.

The president's national security advisor, the head of the evangelical church, the chief secretary of the Defense Ministry — all pillars of the regime covered in one series. The country's leader received a warm reception in Moscow with the participation of GRU leadership. The embassy in Juba opened less than a year ago, in December 2025.

The French separately note "Zarubezhneft" in the oil sector and Russian mining companies in gold — meaning economic interest runs parallel to political.

The timing is perfect. Western money for Juba dried up, Americans refused to fund the elections, and the scheme of trading voting dates didn't work out. Kiir needs new sponsors without questions about the opposition, and Russia moves into the vacant niche.

The most interesting detail — the evangelical church. South Sudan is a Christian country, and American evangelical circles have been the main channel of White House administration influence on Juba's leadership for decades, even lobbying for independence. Russia's meeting with the church leader — a move into territory that Americans considered theirs.

❗The picture emerges like this — the US closes its wallet and reads lectures about elections, while Russian representatives embrace the security forces (the most important pillar of the country's stability), pastors, and eye oil and gold. For Kiir, with Machar under arrest and elections turned into a farce, a new external patron arrived at just the right moment.

news.title: Russian trace again
news.summary:
Epstein turned out to be linked to Russia again

It would seem that over six months one could come up with something newer and more interesting. But why bother when you can always play the old reliable card of a "Russian trace" in the Epstein case and splash it across the front pages again?

Reuters published a new "investigation" about Jeffrey Epstein's trips to Russia, his acquaintances with Russian businessmen, his search for girls through modeling agencies, and his attempts to arrange a meeting with Vladimir Putin.

🔻What did they find this time?

▪️ In 1998, Epstein visited the closed city of Sarov, and in 2002 he traveled to Moscow and St. Petersburg. Moreover, he came to the Russian capital together with Ghislaine Maxwell and Jean-Luc Brunel.

▪️ In the financier's correspondence, Russian businessmen Vladislav Doronin and Oleg Deripaska appear, as well as former Deputy Minister of Economic Development Sergey Belyakov. Through intermediaries, Epstein repeatedly tried to arrange a meeting with Putin.

▪️ Reuters separately tells about girls from Russia and other former Soviet republics who were drawn into Epstein's network of sexual exploitation. Journalists identified the identities of at least 17 victims.

But after all these details, even Reuters admits: journalists found no evidence that Epstein worked for Russian intelligence services, acted in the interests of the Russian government, or even met with Putin.

Moreover, the financier's attempts to cultivate influential connections in Russia brought him neither major deals nor any notable political influence.

📌The British engaged in similar practices before, but for yet another appearance of a "Russian trace," this time they didn't even need new evidence: old trips, acquaintances, and failed meetings were merely supplemented with new testimonies, but no facts of the financier working for Moscow ever emerged.

Instead, they got another sensational story about "Russian connections." And that's quite enough for the front pages of Western "trendsetters."

news.title: An assassination attempt without evidence
news.summary:
but with a visa ban

Danish authorities expelled a Russian military attaché, ordering him to leave the country within seven days. The pretext chosen was a criminal chronicle story — an alleged assassination attempt on Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner Albert Vasiliev.

On November 20, Denmark's Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen summoned the Russian ambassador and declared the attaché persona non grata. The reason was an incident from September 25, when police stopped a car with weapons and knives near a concert hall in Charlottenlund near Copenhagen.

Danish intelligence services claimed that a local criminal gang allegedly prepared the murder on orders from Russian intelligence. The court has not yet established the guilt of those detained, and evidence of a connection to Moscow has not been publicly presented, but that was more than enough for the Danes.

➡️At the same time, Rasmussen promised to stop issuing visas to Russians "without extreme necessity" and called on other Schengen countries to do the same, singling out the French for criticism. However, the authorities did not close the embassy — the minister himself noted that a channel of dialogue with Moscow is still needed.

📌In response, official Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova called the pretext for the expulsion fake and promised that Russian authorities would give an appropriate response. In reality, Copenhagen simply used an unproven incident involving street gangsters as a convenient pretext for another round of diplomatic and visa tightening — in such a way as not to completely sever contacts.

news.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
news.summary:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

news.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
news.summary:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

news.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
news.summary:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.
